$comment: The 50 languages Kagemura ships. 44 are every distinct language the App Store lists apps in (its 50 localizations, March 2026, counting English, French, Spanish and Portuguese once each); 6 are Africa's largest written languages that the store does not list yet. 'wave' is the translation order (largest reach first). 'alsoFor' are device languages that should get this language. 'script' is ISO 15924; Jpan = Han + kana, Kore = Hangul (+ Han). See locales/CLAUDE.md.

languages.name: English
languages.note: Source language. US spelling.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.note: Neutral Latin American Spanish with tú; also served to Spain. Avoid regional slang.

languages.name: Portuguese (Brazil)
languages.note: Brazilian Portuguese with você; also served to Portugal and Africa.

languages.name: French
languages.note: International French with tu; also served to Canada and Africa. Non-breaking space before : ; ! ?

languages.name: German
languages.note: Informal du. Long compounds: keep button labels short.

languages.name: Arabic
languages.note: Modern Standard Arabic, not a dialect. Western digits 0-9 (the game formats numbers).

languages.name: Chinese (Simplified)
languages.note: Mainland conventions. Full-width punctuation.

languages.name: Chinese (Traditional)
languages.note: Taiwan conventions; also served to Hong Kong and Macau. Not a character-by-character conversion of zh-Hans.

languages.name: Japanese
languages.note: The setting is Japanese-flavoured: use natural Japanese for ninja terms (忍者, 道場, 煙玉), not katakana of the English.

languages.name: Korean
languages.note: Polite informal (해요체) for messages; plain nouns for labels.

languages.name: Indonesian
languages.note: Friendly standard Indonesian with kamu.

languages.name: Russian
languages.note: Informal ты. Plural forms matter (one/few/many).

languages.name: Hindi
languages.note: Everyday Hindi, not Sanskritised. Address the player as आप with polite imperatives (रद्द करें), the convention of Hindi software; this overrides the glossary's informal-you rule, because तुम reads as talking down to many adult players. The player's gender is unknown and placeholders have no fixed gender: prefer phrasings where nothing agrees with them (ने constructions, passives, noun phrases such as आपका हमला हो चुका है); only where Hindi has no natural neutral form, use the honorific default of Hindi software (आप … सकते हैं). Plural one covers 0 and 1. Nukta letters are stored as base letter + ़ (NFC). End sentences with । and keep ? and !. Western digits only (the game formats numbers in the Indian grouping). Game words players say in English may stay English, written in Devanagari; store and platform brands stay in Latin letters.

languages.name: Turkish
languages.note: Informal sen. Suffixes attach to placeholders: rephrase so {n} needs no suffix.

languages.name: Vietnamese
languages.note: Full diacritics (precomposed, NFC).

languages.name: Thai
languages.note: No spaces between words; the UI breaks lines with the browser's Thai line breaking.

languages.name: Italian
languages.note: Informal tu.

languages.name: Polish
languages.note: Informal ty. Plural forms matter (one/few/many).

languages.name: Ukrainian
languages.note: Translate from English, never from Russian.

languages.name: Dutch
languages.note: Informal je. Also served to Flemish (nl-BE).

languages.name: Malay
languages.note: Malaysian Malay. Not Indonesian: vocabulary differs.

languages.name: Bangla
languages.note: Standard colloquial Bangla (Bangladesh and West Bengal).

languages.name: Urdu
languages.note: Standard Urdu in Arabic script (the phone's Nastaliq or Naskh font draws it).

languages.name: Swahili
languages.note: Standard Swahili (Kiswahili sanifu), understood across East Africa.

languages.name: Hausa
languages.note: Boko (Latin) script with the hooked letters ɓ ɗ ƙ ƴ. Nigeria and Niger.

languages.name: Yoruba
languages.note: Full tone marks and dot-below letters (ẹ ọ ṣ), NFC.

languages.name: Amharic
languages.note: Ge'ez (Ethiopic) script. Ethiopia.

languages.name: Zulu
languages.note: Standard Zulu. South Africa.

languages.name: Igbo
languages.note: Standard Igbo with dot-below vowels (ị ọ ụ) and ṅ. Nigeria.

languages.name: Tamil
languages.note: Tamil words run long: keep labels short.

languages.name: Malayalam
languages.note: Words run long: keep labels short.

languages.name: Punjabi
languages.note: Gurmukhi script (India).

languages.name: Romanian
languages.note: Comma-below ș ț, not cedilla.

languages.name: Hebrew
languages.note: No niqqud. Gender-neutral phrasing where possible.

languages.name: Finnish
languages.note: Case endings attach to placeholders: rephrase so {n} needs none.

languages.name: Norwegian
languages.note: Bokmål.

languages.name: Slovenian
languages.note: Has a dual: plural forms one/two/few/other.
